page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head and page number at the top and a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: illis aduena,& sociabuntur ad domum Ia-cob. Tollent eos populi, & introducet eos ad locum suum, & hæreditare facient eos domum Israel super terram Domini, ut sint serui & ancillæ (Domini:) & erunt capientes eos qui se ceperant, dominabunturque in exastores suos. Et erit in die qua tibi requiem dederit Dominus à labore tuo, & à tremore tuo, atq; à dura seruitute, qua oppressio facta est in te: & sumes parabolam hanc contra regem Babel, & dices: Quomodo quieuit exastor, cessauit aurum tributarium? Confregit Dominus sceptrum impiorum, uirgam dominantiû, percutientem populos in indignatione plaga indesinente: dominantem in ira gentibus, persecutionem passis (ab eo) absque ulla misera tione. Quieuit & coticuit omnis terra, aperientes (os suum) ad laudem. Sed & abietes lætatæ sunt super te, & cedri Libani, à tempore quo iacuisti, nec ascendit succisor contra nos. Infernus desubtus commotus est propter te, in occursum aduetus tui, excitauit ppter[?] te mortuos & omnes directo res terræ, suscitauit de foliis suis omnes reges gentium. Omnes ipsi respondebunt tibi, & dicent ad te: Etiam tu infirmatus es sicut

page.notes: Long s normalised to plain s throughout (e.g. "fuum" as suum, "eft" as est, "funt" as sunt), and j/i and u/v corrected per the rules. "ppter" is a doubtful abbreviation mark and is flagged [?]. "tione" and "tione" break at the line end ("misera / tione") is kept as printed. "exastores" and "exastor" follow the printed "ft" ligature, read as s + t, so this may be a misreading of "exactor". "dominantiû" carries a macron-u as printed. The printed "ficut" at the lower right is the catchword, not text. Page number read as 138.
